events.article: Considerando on information about refugio for US deportees admitted on humanitarian grounds
events.what_changed: Found that about 200 US deportees admitted on humanitarian grounds were not shown to have been told from entry that they could seek refuge, and held that this injured their rights. It is a fact-specific finding with a 'take note' for future humanitarian admissions. It sets no general duty to advise before expulsion or rejection, so it is practice evidence and does not change the protection answer.
events.passage: No se demuestra; sin embargo, que tal información se transmitiera a las personas tuteladas desde el momento de su ingreso. [...] El lapso en el cual esta obligación se incumplió implicó la lesión de los derechos de las personas que eventualmente tuvieran acceso a la figura [...] Tome nota la autoridad recurrida de lo dispuesto en esta sentencia a los efectos de eventuales autorizaciones de ingreso de personas por razones de humanidad.

answers.implementation_then_now: Not rated on either date, because the law has no duty to advise of asylum before rejection or deportation. For the record: in 2025, HRW reported that deportees said they had repeatedly stated an intention to seek asylum, and the Sala Constitucional found they had not been informed from the moment of entry. Nothing comparable was found for 2022, but the rating stays Does Not Apply.

events.article: Habeas corpus on US deportees at CATEM-Sur
events.what_changed: The Sala partly upheld a habeas corpus for about 200 third-country deportees held at CATEM under a collective humanitarian resolution (D.JUR-0057-02-2025-JM) and ordered individual decisions. This is a documented breach in practice; it does not change the law.
events.passage: La resolución D. JUR-0057-02-2025-JM, indicó que la permanencia podrá ser autorizada por una única vez y tendrá validez por un plazo de treinta días naturales, a efecto de que las personas beneficiadas puedan hacer abandono del país.

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: the US State Department reports covering 2021 and 2023 describe a functioning asylum and migration system. They record no pattern of arbitrary or collective expulsions; the main problems they note are backlogs. That supports Usually, though the evidence is thin and indirect. 2026: in the US-deportee episode of 2025, people were held under a collective resolution without individual decisions, and the Sala Constitucional corrected this through habeas corpus. This is a serious but isolated breach that the courts remedied. No systematic shift was found, so the rating stays Usually.

events.article: Habeas corpus on US deportees at CATEM-Sur
events.what_changed: Review of the deportees' situation came only through habeas corpus. They had been held under a collective resolution rather than individual proceedings with a hearing. This is practice evidence of a gap; it does not change the law.
events.passage: Se consideró que la autorización de permanencia es en el CATEM Sur, y al tener ese proceso un fin de tránsito por nuestro país se estimó fundamental tener ubicadas a estas personas para acelerar el proceso de continuación de viaje.

answers.implementation_then_now: In both periods, expulsion of lawful residents carries a hearing and an appeal with suspensive effect. Deportation of irregular migrants is summary (art. 207) and cannot be appealed administratively (art. 222), so review depends on habeas corpus. For 2022, the US DOS reports show a functioning system and no documented pattern of denied hearings; this evidence is indirect. For 2025, the CATEM episode shows deportees processed collectively without individual hearings until the Sala intervened. This is consistent with the existing mixed rating rather than a shift, so the rating stays Sometimes; Usually on both dates.

practice_sources.title: 2021 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Costa Rica (US DOS)
2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Costa Rica (US DOS)

answers.sourcing_note: Arts. 65, 207, 209, 210, 215, 216, 217 and 222 of Ley 8764 and art. 40 of the Regulation were read in the current consolidated text; none carries an amendment note, so they are unchanged since 2009/2011. Practice evidence for around 2022 is indirect, and specific data on deportation hearings were not found.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The Yes rests on the oral hearing before the DGME in deportation (art. 209). Review by a separate body exists only for expulsion and refugee cases (art. 222 bars appeals against rejection and deportation). A stricter reviewer could treat irregular migrants as uncovered.
answers.notes: The FIDH report cited in the starting answer predates the window and was not opened.
